# 1. Pulls the `## [x.y.z]` section for the given version out of the app's `CHANGELOG.md` and turns it into *What's New* texts: one for App Store Connect (4000 chars max) and one per locale for Google Play (500 chars max!!), written to `fastlane/metadata/...` so `deliver` and `supply` pick them up.
# 2. Plots installs and crash-free sessions for the launch retro from the CSV exports in `data/` (the handbook page *Store metadata & screenshots* says where to download them).
#
# Lines starting with `Internal:` in the changelog are dropped, and so are issue numbers like `(#488)`.
#
# * needs `pandas` + `matplotlib`, nothing else
# * the Play limit is per locale and counts **characters, not bytes**   (an emoji is 1, or 2 with a variation selector... don't ask)

# %%
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| warning:   False
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
import textwrap
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
LIMITS = {"app_store": 4000, "google_play": 500}
APPS = {
    "glowtide": {"name": "Glowtide", "changelog": ROOT / "games/glowtide/CHANGELOG.md", "locales": ["en-US", "de-DE", "ja", "ko", "pt-BR"]},
    "sprout":   {"name": "Sprout", "changelog": ROOT / "apps/CHANGELOG-sprout.md", "locales": ["en-US", "de-DE"]},
}

# %%
#| label: changelog-parsing
#| code-fold : true
#| code-summary: "Show the changelog parser"
SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"^## \[?(?P<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\]?\s+[-–(]\s*(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", re.M)


@dataclass
class Release:
    version: str
    date: date
    body: str

    @property
    def bullets(self) -> list[str]:
        out = []
        for line in self.body.splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if line[:2] in ("- ", "* ", "+ ") and not line[2:].startswith("Internal:"):
                out.append(re.sub(r"\s*\(#\d+(, #\d+)*\)", "", line[2:]))
        return out


def find_release(changelog: Path, version: str) -> Release:
    text = changelog.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    matches = list(SECTION_RE.finditer(text))
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        if m["version"] == version:
            end = matches[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(matches) else len(text)
            return Release(version, date.fromisoformat(m["date"]), text[m.end():end])
    sys.exit(f"version {version} not found in {changelog}")


# fmt: markdown
APP_STORE_FOOTER = """
Thanks for playing! If you enjoy the update, a short review helps a tiny studio more than you would think.   Found a bug? *Settings → Help → Send feedback* attaches your device info automatically.
"""

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
PLAY_INTRO = """
New in this version. Full notes at lanternfish.studio/changes. Thanks for playing!
"""

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = r"""
Examples:

    store_report.py --app glowtide --version 1.8.1 --write
    store_report.py --app sprout --version 3.2.0 --skip '^\s*Internal:'

The `--skip` pattern is a Python regex matched against each bullet *after* the marker is removed, so `^\s*` is usually what you want.
"""


def whats_new(app: str, rel: Release, store: str) -> str:
    limit = LIMITS[store]
    name = APPS[app]["name"]
    bullets = "\n".join(f"• {b}" for b in rel.bullets)
    if store == "app_store":
        text = f"{name} {rel.version}\n\n{bullets}\n\n{APP_STORE_FOOTER.strip()}"
    else:
        text = f"{PLAY_INTRO.strip()}\n{bullets}"
    if len(text) > limit:
        text = textwrap.shorten(text, width=limit - 1, placeholder="…")
    return text


def discord_post(app: str, rel: Release, build: int) -> str:
    name = APPS[app]["name"]
    # fmt: markdown
    return f"""
**{name} {rel.version}** (build {build}) is on its way to the stores :tada:

{chr(10).join('- ' + b for b in rel.bullets[:6])}

* App Store: phased release over 7 days, starts after review
* Google Play: staged rollout, 5% → 20% → 50% → 100%
Full changelog: <https://github.com/lanternfish/studio/blob/main/games/glowtide/CHANGELOG.md>
"""


# fmt: json
SAMPLE_CRASHLYTICS_ROW = """
{"os":"iOS 18.1","app_version":"1.8.0 (1800412)","sessions":48211,"crash_free_sessions":0.9971,"top_issue":null}
"""

# %% [markdown]
# fmt: markdown
# ## Launch numbers
#
# Installs are *first-time downloads* (App Store "First-Time Downloads", Play "Device acquisitions"), so re-downloads and updates are not in here.  Crash-free numbers come from Crashlytics and lag about 24 h behind.

# %%
#| label: fig-installs
#| fig-cap: "Daily first-time installs per store, first 14 days after launch"
#| fig-alt: "Line chart with two lines, App Store and Google Play. Both spike on launch day at about 4,100 and 6,300 installs and settle around 1,200 per day after day 10."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height:   4
#| layout: [[1],
#|   [1]]
def plot_installs(csv: Path, days: int = 14):
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    import pandas as pd

    df = pd.read_csv(csv, parse_dates=["date"])
    first = df["date"].min()
    df = df[df["date"] < first + pd.Timedelta(days=days)]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
    for store, grp in df.groupby("store"):
        ax.plot(grp["date"], grp["first_time_downloads"], label=store.replace("_", " ").title())
    ax.set_ylabel("first-time installs")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    return fig


# %%
#| label: tbl-crash-free
#| tbl-cap: Crash-free sessions by OS version (min. 500 sessions)
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
#| tags: [ report,crashlytics ]
#| params:
#|     min_sessions: 500
#|     platforms:
#|     - ios
#|     - android
def crash_table(csv: Path, min_sessions: int = 500) -> str:
    import pandas as pd

    df = pd.read_csv(csv)
    df = df[df["sessions"] >= min_sessions].sort_values("crash_free_sessions")
    rows = [f"| {r.os} | {r.app_version} | {r.sessions:,} | {r.crash_free_sessions:.2%} |" for r in df.itertuples()]
    return "\n".join(["| OS | build | sessions | crash-free |", "|---|---|--:|--:|", *rows])


# %%
#| label: cli
#| eval: false
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0], epilog=EPILOG, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--app", choices=sorted(APPS), required=True)
    p.add_argument("--version", required=True, help="semver, e.g. 1.8.1")
    p.add_argument("--build", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="write into fastlane/metadata instead of printing")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)

    rel = find_release(APPS[args.app]["changelog"], args.version)
    ios_txt = whats_new(args.app, rel, "app_store")
    play_txt = whats_new(args.app, rel, "google_play")
    if not args.write:
        print(ios_txt, "", play_txt, "", discord_post(args.app, rel, args.build), sep="\n")
        return 0
    meta = ROOT / "fastlane" / "metadata"
    (meta / "ios" / "en-US" / "release_notes.txt").write_text(ios_txt + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    code = int(args.version.replace(".", "")) if args.build == 0 else args.build
    for loc in APPS[args.app]["locales"]:
        out = meta / "android" / loc / "changelogs" / f"{code}.txt"
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if loc == "en-US" or not out.exists():
            out.write_text(play_txt + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# reviews_digest.R -------------------------------------------------------------
# Weekly store review digest for Sprout + Glowtide.
#
#   Rscript analysis/reviews_digest.R 2026-W46
#   quarto render analysis/reviews_digest.R -P week:2026-W46    # html report, uses the #| blocks
#
# Pulls reviews from App Store Connect + Google Play, tags them, posts a summary to
# Discord and opens GitHub issues for reviews that mention crashes.   -- priya, 2026-03

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: FALSE
#| include : false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(stringr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(httr2)
  library(glue)
})

args  <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
week  <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else strftime(Sys.Date() - 7, "%G-W%V")
since <- ISOweek::ISOweek2date(paste0(week, "-1"))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Where the reviews come from
#
# * **App Store**: App Store Connect API, `GET /v1/apps/{id}/customerReviews?sort=-createdDate`, 200 per page.  We page until we hit a review older than `since`.
# * **Google Play**: `reviews.list` from the Android Publisher API. It only returns reviews **with text** from the last 7 days, so if the cron job doesn't run for a week those reviews are gone for good (happened in March, see #298)
# *  Steam reviews for Glowtide are not pulled yet.
#
# Star ratings *without* text only show up in the aggregate numbers, which we don't use here.

APPS <- tribble(
  ~app,       ~store,        ~id,
  "sprout",   "app_store",   "6449021137",
  "sprout",   "google_play", "studio.lanternfish.sprout",
  "glowtide", "app_store",   "6452210980",
  "glowtide", "google_play", "studio.lanternfish.glowtide"
)

# Fetching ---------------------------------------------------------------------

#' App Store Connect JWT (ES256, valid for 20 minutes)
#' @noRd
asc_token <- function() {
  claim <- jose::jwt_claim(iss = Sys.getenv("ASC_ISSUER_ID"), aud = "appstoreconnect-v1", exp = as.integer(Sys.time()) + 1200)
  jose::jwt_encode_sig(claim, key = Sys.getenv("ASC_KEY_P8"), header = list(kid = Sys.getenv("ASC_KEY_ID")))
}

fetch_app_store <- function(id, since) {
  req <- request(glue("https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com/v1/apps/{id}/customerReviews")) |>
    req_url_query(sort = "-createdDate", limit = 200, include = "response") |>
    req_auth_bearer_token(asc_token())
  pages <- list()
  repeat {
    resp <- req |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
    page <- map_dfr(resp$data, \(r) tibble(
      review_id = r$id, rating = r$attributes$rating, title = r$attributes$title,
      body = r$attributes$body, territory = r$attributes$territory, version = NA_character_,
      created = ymd_hms(r$attributes$createdDate),
      has_reply = !is.null(r$relationships$response$data)
    ))
    pages <- c(pages, list(page))
    if (nrow(page) == 0 || min(page$created) < since || is.null(resp$links[["next"]])) break
    req <- request(resp$links[["next"]]) |> req_auth_bearer_token(asc_token())
  }
  bind_rows(pages) |> filter(created >= since)
}

fetch_google_play <- function(id, since) {
  token <- gargle::credentials_service_account(
    scopes = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher",
    path   = Sys.getenv("PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON")
  )
  resp <- request(glue("https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/androidpublisher/v3/applications/{id}/reviews")) |>
    req_url_query(maxResults = 100) |>
    req_auth_bearer_token(token$credentials$access_token) |>
    req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
  map_dfr(resp$reviews, \(r) {
    c1 <- r$comments[[1]]$userComment
    tibble(
      review_id = r$reviewId, rating = c1$starRating, title = NA_character_, body = str_trim(c1$text),
      territory = c1$reviewerLanguage, version = c1$appVersionName %||% NA_character_,
      created = as_datetime(as.numeric(c1$lastModified$seconds)),
      has_reply = length(r$comments) > 1
    )
  }) |> filter(created >= since)
}

#| label: fetch
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr week
reviews <- APPS |>
  mutate(data = map2(store, id, \(store, id) switch(store,
    app_store   = fetch_app_store(id, since),
    google_play = fetch_google_play(id, since)
  ))) |>
  select(-id) |>
  unnest(data)

# Tagging ----------------------------------------------------------------------
CRASH_WORDS <- c("crash", "freez", "absturz", "stürzt", "落ち", "강제 종료", "trava", "fecha sozinho")

tag_review <- function(text) {
  text <- str_to_lower(coalesce(text, ""))
  case_when(
    str_detect(text, str_c(CRASH_WORDS, collapse = "|")) ~ "crash",
    str_detect(text, "subscri|abo|price|preis|expensive|teuer|課金|サブスク") ~ "money",
    str_detect(text, "sync|icloud|backup|lost my|verloren")                  ~ "sync",
    .default = "other"
  )
}
reviews <- reviews |> mutate(tag = tag_review(paste(title, body)))

#| label: fig-rating-trend
#| fig-cap: "7-day rolling mean rating by store"
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the seven day rolling mean star rating for Sprout on iOS and Android since June 2026. iOS stays between 4.5 and 4.7. Android drops from 4.4 to 4.1 after the 3.1.0 release on Aug 19 and recovers to 4.4 after 3.1.2."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-asp: .5
#| fig-format: [png, svg]
reviews |>
  filter(app == "sprout") |>
  group_by(store, day = as_date(created)) |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating), n = n(), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(rolling = slider::slide_dbl(rating, mean, .before = 6)) |>
  ggplot(aes(day, rolling, colour = store)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 5)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "rating (7-day mean)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Posting ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# fmt: markdown
discord_template <- r"(
**Weekly review digest** — {week}

Sprout: **{avg_sprout_ios}★** on iOS and **{avg_sprout_android}★** on Android.   Glowtide: **{avg_glowtide}★** across both stores.
{n_total} new reviews this week, {n_unanswered} of them still without a developer reply.

Top tags: {top_tags}
)"

# fmt: markdown
footer_md <- "
*Generated by `analysis/reviews_digest.R` for {week}.   Ratings are 1–5 stars; 'unanswered' means there is no developer response in App Store Connect / Play Console yet.*
"

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
issue_template <- R"---[
## Crash mentioned in a store review

Auto-filed by `analysis/reviews_digest.R`. The review below mentions a crash or a freeze. Please find the matching Crashlytics issue (filter by app version {version} and, if the store gives us one, the device model) and link it here before closing. If it is a duplicate, close it with the `duplicate` label so the script doesn't file it again next week.

> {body}
>
> — {store}, {territory}, {rating}★, {format(created, '%Y-%m-%d')}

- [ ] matching Crashlytics issue linked
- [ ] fixed in a build (add the version to the changelog entry)
]---"

avg_rating <- function(a, s = c("app_store", "google_play")) {
  reviews |> filter(app == a, store %in% s) |> pull(rating) |> mean() |> round(2)
}

msg <- glue(
  discord_template,
  avg_sprout_ios     = avg_rating("sprout", "app_store"),
  avg_sprout_android = avg_rating("sprout", "google_play"),
  avg_glowtide       = avg_rating("glowtide"),
  n_total      = nrow(reviews),
  n_unanswered = sum(!reviews$has_reply),
  top_tags     = reviews |> count(tag, sort = TRUE) |> head(3) |> glue_data("{tag} ({n})") |> glue_collapse(", ")
)

#| label: post
#| eval: !expr '!interactive()'
#| output:    false
if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("DISCORD_WEBHOOK"))) {
  request(Sys.getenv("DISCORD_WEBHOOK")) |>
    req_body_json(list(content = paste(msg, glue(footer_md), sep = "\n"))) |>
    req_perform()
}

crash_reviews <- reviews |> filter(tag == "crash", rating <= 2)

---
title: "Sprout — Q3 2026 ratings, reviews & the 3.2 paywall test"
author: "Priya Raman, Jun Watanabe"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    code_folding: hide
    df_print: paged
  github_document: default
params:
  quarter: "2026-Q3"
  min_reviews: 20
  paywall_test_id: pw-annual-first
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
    canonical: true
    references:
      location: section
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.retina = 2)
library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(gt)
reviews <- readRDS(here::here("data", "reviews_2026Q3.rds"))
paywall <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", paste0("paywall_", params$paywall_test_id, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE)
n_reviews <- nrow(reviews)
```

## Summary

Sprout ended Q3 2026 with an average rating of 4.62 on the App Store (n = 1,184 new ratings) and 4.31 on Google Play (n = 2,907), i.e. roughly flat on iOS vs. Q2 and down 0.12 on Android. The Android dip is almost entirely explained by v3.1.0, which shipped on Aug. 19 with a widget bug on Samsung One UI 6.1 devices; after the fix in v3.1.2 (Aug. 27) the 7-day average went back to approx. 4.4 within ten days. We also ran the paywall test `pw-annual-first` from Sept. 1 to Sept. 28, which showed the annual plan ($39.99/yr, i.e. ~33% cheaper than 12 × $4.99) before the monthly one. It increased trial starts by 11.8% (95% CI 4.1%–19.9%) and did not measurably change the number of 1★ reviews mentioning "subscription", "price", "Abo" etc. Recommendation: ship variant B to 100% in v3.2.1 and keep monitoring refunds through Q4.

There were `r n_reviews` reviews with text in total. Of these, 412 were in English, 233 in German and the rest spread over 9 other locales (mostly ja, ko, pt-BR and fr). Dr. Ana Pereira (our pt-BR translator, a.k.a. the reason Sprout has 4.8★ in Brazil) went through the Portuguese ones by hand; everything else was tagged with the keyword rules in `R/tag_reviews.R`, v2.3. The rules are deliberately simple. They miss sarcasm, e.g. "great, another subscription app..." is tagged as positive, but a manual check of 200 random reviews found only 6 mislabeled ones (3.0%).

## Ratings by version

```{r ratings-by-version, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Average star rating by app version, iOS and Android. Versions with fewer than 20 ratings are hidden."}
reviews |>
  group_by(platform, version) |>
  filter(n() >= params$min_reviews) |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(version, rating, fill = platform)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(3.5, 5))
```

Fig. 1 shows the average rating per version for both platforms. Versions with fewer than `r params$min_reviews` ratings are hidden, because e.g. v3.0.3 (a two-day hotfix) only got 7 ratings on iOS. Note that Apple lets users keep their rating across versions unless they change it, so the iOS numbers lag behind the actual experience by approx. 2–3 weeks; Google does __not__ do that. In the U.S. App Store the share of 5★ ratings went from 71.4% to 74.0%. Most of them arrived after the in-app rating prompt moved from "after 3 days" to "after the 5th watered plant", which we shipped in v3.1.0 (see PR #388). Was it worth it? Probably, yes!

The version breakdown also shows something we did not expect: v3.1.1 on Android has a _lower_ average (3.94) than v3.1.0 (4.02), even though it fixed nothing and broke nothing. It turns out v3.1.1 was the version most people were on when the widget bug hit them, since Play updates roll out over approx. 7 days and many users updated straight from 3.0.x to 3.1.1. In other words the ratings are attached to the version installed at review time, not the version that caused the problem. We'll keep that in mind before blaming a release for a dip again.

## The paywall test

The test ran on new installs only, split 50/50 by a hash of the Firebase installation ID, with n = 8,417 in variant A (monthly first) and n = 8,392 in variant B (annual first). Trial-start rate went from 6.43% to 7.19%. That's +0.76 pp, or +11.8% relative, p = 0.004 using a two-sided two-proportion z-test[^method]. Conversion from trial to paid after 7 days is still preliminary: 41.0% vs. 42.3%, and the CI is wide (approx. −2.9 to +5.5 pp), so we can't say much yet. Revenue per install in the first 28 days was €0.61 vs. €0.74 on Google Play and $0.83 vs. $0.97 on the App Store, before Apple's/Google's 15% cut (Small Business Program).

| Variant | Installs | Trial starts | Rate | Paid after 7 d |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A — monthly first | 8,417 | 541 | 6.43% | 41.0% |
| B — annual first | 8,392 | 603 | 7.19% | 42.3% |

A few caveats, roughly in order of how much they worry us:

1. The test overlapped with the back-to-school sale on Sept. 9–15 (−30% on the annual plan in the U.S., U.K., CA and AU only). Both variants got the sale, but variant B shows the annual price first, so it likely benefited more. Excluding that week, the uplift shrinks to +8.9% and is no longer significant at the 1% level (p = 0.021).
2. Android users on One UI 6.1 were over-represented in A after Sept. 20 because of a bucketing bug in v3.1.3 (fixed in v3.1.4, see `RemoteConfigClient.kt`, l. 212). It affected approx. 300 installs. We re-ran the analysis without them and nothing changed beyond the 2nd decimal.
3. Seven days is short for a subscription app. Our trial is 7 days, so "paid after 7 d" really means "did not cancel during the trial", nothing more. Refunds typically come in weeks 2–6.

> "I'd pay for this if it didn't nag me every time I open it. Update: the new screen is fine, it only shows up once. 4 stars." — Google Play review, en-GB, Sept. 14, v3.1.3

```{r paywall-ci}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
ci <- prop.test(x = c(603, 541), n = c(8392, 8417), correct = FALSE)$conf.int
cat(sprintf("Absolute difference in trial-start rate: %.2f to %.2f pp (95%% CI).", 100 * ci[1], 100 * ci[2]))
```

## Reviews mentioning the subscription

We tagged 1★ and 2★ reviews with the keyword list from last quarter (subscription, Abo, 課金, price, Preis, expensive, teuer, etc.). The share of low ratings mentioning money went from 22% in Q2 to 19% in Q3, which is within the noise for n ≈ 340. Jun read all 61 of them; the most common complaint (17 reviews) is that the free tier only allows 5 plants, not the price itself. Mr. Lund suggested raising the limit to 8 plants. That's a product decision rather than a stats one, so it goes to the planning meeting on Oct. 6 at 10 a.m. CET.

* iOS: 1★/2★ share 6.2% → 5.8%. Most complaints are about iCloud sync (fixed in v3.2.0) and the widget not updating on iOS 18.0.x. The widget issue is Apple's (FB15022183) and it's fixed in iOS 18.1.
* Android: 1★/2★ share 9.9% → 11.4%, mostly v3.1.0 widget crashes. Excluding Aug. 19–27 it's 8.7%, i.e. better than Q2.
   Samsung devices account for 58% of those, vs. 41% of our Android installs overall.

## Next steps

- Ship variant B (annual first) to 100% in v3.2.1 and freeze the paywall until Dec. 1 so the refund numbers stay clean.
- Re-run this report for Q4 with the same `min_reviews` threshold. Black Friday (Nov. 27) falls into Q4, so expect the trial-start rate to be inflated for approx. one week; we'll report it with and without that week, like the back-to-school sale above.
- Ask the ja translator about "課金" vs. "サブスク" in the keyword list. It might be missing ~10% of the relevant reviews, which would matter more than anything else in this section.
- Reply to the 40 unanswered 1★ reviews from Aug. 19–27 (template in the handbook, under *Support → Store replies*). Replies can move a rating: in Q2, 14 of 52 users we replied to updated their rating, on average by +1.6★.

[^method]: Two-proportion z-test with pooled variance, computed with `prop.test(correct = FALSE)`. We did not correct for multiple comparisons since there is only one primary metric (trial-start rate). Secondary metrics are reported for context only, e.g. paid conversion, revenue per install etc.
